rationale: Retain the newly inspected asynchronous worker boundary and its unresolved snapshot/application correspondence before constructing any safety obligation.

feedback.answered: The asynchronous contract requires FIFO per local destination but explicitly permits arbitrary ordering between LocalAppendThread and LocalApplyThread. Its example sends snapshots to the append worker and entries to the apply worker, with responses after each operation. Actual in-repository InteractionEnv routing likewise retains independent AppendWork and ApplyWork queues. processAppend applies a snapshot to MemoryStorage; processApply independently invokes RawNode.ApplyConfChange for each configuration entry and appends an appender-state snapshot to History. The storage wrapper overrides Snapshot reads from History but inherits ApplySnapshot from MemoryStorage; the read implementation does not supply a cross-worker cancellation or covered-prefix filter. These are test-driver observations, not evidence about a production embedding. Core restore installs ConfState immediately, while previously dispatched application messages are caller-owned. The exact unresolved contract is whether a caller must discard or otherwise reconcile already dispatched configuration entries covered by a later installed snapshot before invoking ApplyConfChange. The acquired asynchronous instructions do not explain that coordination. No failing history or violation is asserted.
remaining: Trace a legal producer prefix in which a committed configuration is already dispatched to the apply worker and a strictly newer snapshot is actually accepted before that worker completes; matching-log fast-forward may prevent full restore and must be investigated.

If full restore is reachable, determine whether invoking the older entry is contract-compliant or requires a caller-side covered-prefix rule, before attributing membership or application consequences.
feedback.rationale: The newer-snapshot marker protection does not settle caller-owned work already dispatched. The next discriminator is full-restore reachability: a snapshot matching an existing entry only advances commit and does not reinstall configuration. Testing an arbitrary snapshot against fabricated state would skip this limiting premise.
